Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides bank-financed margin money subsidy to set up brand-new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector
Financial Benefit Details: Margin money subsidy of 15%-35% of project cost; project cost ceiling Rs. 50 lakh (manufacturing) / Rs. 20 lakh (service); 35% subsidy (rural) / 25% (urban) for SC/ST/Women/PH/Minorities/Ex-servicemen/NER, 15%-25% for general category
Age Eligibility: 18 years minimum; no upper limit specified
Main Benefits: Margin money subsidy on a bank loan for setting up a new micro-enterprise; no separate collateral required up to prescribed limits under CGTMSE linkage

Scheme Name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
Social Category Eligibility: Any (women-owned units get enhanced guarantee coverage)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Guarantees loans extended by banks/NBFCs to MSEs, enabling entrepreneurs to access credit without collateral or third-party guarantee
Financial Benefit Details: Guarantee coverage of 75%-85% of loan amount (higher for micro enterprises, women entrepreneurs, NER/hilly states); maximum credit facility eligible for guarantee raised to Rs. 10 crore per borrower effective 1 April 2025; nominal Annual Guarantee Fee starting around 0.37% p.a.
Main Benefits: Enables collateral-free bank credit for MSEs by guaranteeing a large share of the loan amount to the lender

Social Category Eligibility: Any (women constitute a majority of borrowers; special outreach to SC/ST and minorities)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides collateral-free loans to start or expand micro and small businesses
Financial Benefit Details: Shishu: up to Rs. 50,000; Kishor: Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5 lakh; Tarun: Rs. 5 lakh to Rs. 10 lakh; Tarun Plus: Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 20 lakh (introduced Union Budget 2024-25, available only to entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid a Tarun loan)
Main Benefits: Collateral-free, no-processing-fee loans up to Rs. 20 lakh for micro and small enterprises across four graduated categories

Gender Eligibility: Women (also open to men from SC/ST category)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides composite bank loans for setting up a new enterprise in manufacturing, services, trading or agri-allied activities
Financial Benefit Details: Composite loan (term loan plus working capital) of Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 1 crore; credit guarantee cover available through the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Stand-Up India (up to 80% coverage as per bank norms)
Main Benefits: Bank loans of Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 1 crore for new enterprises with credit guarantee support and handholding assistance

Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Guarantees term loans, working capital and venture debt extended to startups by banks, NBFCs and Alternative Investment Funds
Financial Benefit Details: Guarantee cover of up to Rs. 20 crore per borrower (doubled from the earlier Rs. 10 crore limit); guarantee coverage of 75%-85%
Age Eligibility: Not specified at individual level; enterprise must qualify as a 'startup' under DPIIT norms (generally recognised for up to 10 years from incorporation)
State / Geographic Eligibility: All India (implemented in 20+ states and union territories as of late 2025)
Main Benefits: Collateral-free debt financing of up to Rs. 20 crore for DPIIT-recognised startups

Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides seed-stage grant and debt funding to startups through approved incubators
Financial Benefit Details: Up to Rs. 20 lakh as a grant for proof of concept, prototype development or product trials; up to Rs. 50 lakh as debt/convertible instruments for market entry and commercialisation, disbursed through eligible incubators
Age Eligibility: Not applicable at individual level; startup entity age typically under 2 years
Main Benefits: Early-stage grant and debt funding for prototype development, validation and market entry

Social Category Eligibility: Any (open to all artisans in the notified trades regardless of caste category)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides formal recognition, skill training, modern toolkit support and collateral-free loans to artisan micro-businesses
Financial Benefit Details: Rs. 15,000 toolkit incentive (e-voucher); collateral-free loans up to Rs. 3 lakh in two tranches at concessional interest (around 5%); Rs. 500/day training stipend; Re. 1 per digital transaction incentive (capped at 100 transactions/month)
Age Eligibility: 18 years minimum; no upper limit specified
Main Benefits: Recognition certificate, skill training, toolkit grant, collateral-free loans, digital transaction incentives and marketing support for traditional artisans

Scheme Name: PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides working capital loans to street vendors to restart or grow their vending business
Financial Benefit Details: Progressive collateral-free working capital loans across three tranches (reported figures vary across official communications, broadly in the range of Rs. 10,000-15,000 for the first tranche, up to Rs. 20,000-25,000 for the second, and up to Rs. 50,000 for the third); 7% interest subsidy on timely repayment; digital-payment cashback of up to about Rs. 1,200/year
Main Benefits: Collateral-free working capital loans in progressive tranches with an interest subsidy and digital-payment cashback incentives

Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides business development support, mentorship, market linkages and facilitates access to credit, technology and training for SC/ST entrepreneurs
Financial Benefit Details: Not applicable directly; the Hub is a facilitation and support ecosystem that connects entrepreneurs to other credit and procurement schemes rather than disbursing funds itself
Main Benefits: Mentorship, networking with investors and government agencies, market linkages and overall business development support

Scheme Name: NSFDC Term Loan / Micro Credit Finance Scheme
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides concessional term loans for setting up self-employment ventures and small businesses
Financial Benefit Details: Term loans of up to 90% of project cost routed through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs); Micro Credit Finance component provides loans up to Rs. 1.25 lakh (project cost up to about Rs. 1.4 lakh) at concessional interest around 6.5% p.a., repayable quarterly over 3 years
Main Benefits: Concessional term loans enabling SC entrepreneurs to set up income-generating micro-enterprises

Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides concessional term loans for setting up or expanding minority-owned businesses, including working-capital support for artisans
Financial Benefit Details: Credit Line 1 and Credit Line 2 offer term loans up to about Rs. 10-20 lakh depending on the component; interest rates for artisans around 4%-6% p.a. (lower for women); financing pattern is roughly NMDFC:SCA:beneficiary in the range of 90:5:5 to 90:10
Income Limit: Below double the poverty line (benchmark similar to Rs. 3 lakh/year used by comparable corporations; confirm current NMDFC-specific limit)
Main Benefits: Concessional term loans and micro-financing for minority entrepreneurs, artisans and women's Self-Help Groups

Scheme Name: NBCFDC New Swarnima Scheme for Women
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides concessional loans to women from backward classes to start or expand small businesses
Financial Benefit Details: Loan up to Rs. 1,00,000 at 5% p.a. interest; NBCFDC loan component covers about 95% of project cost
Income Limit: Below double the poverty line (older circular cites Rs. 81,000/year rural and Rs. 1,03,000/year urban; verify current limit on official website as this may have been revised)
Main Benefits: Low-interest (5% p.a.) loans specifically for women entrepreneurs from backward classes

Social Category Eligibility: Any (priority to SC/ST/OBC/Minorities; caste/community certificate required where claimed)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides a credit-linked subsidy for establishing new coir manufacturing units
Financial Benefit Details: Project cost up to Rs. 10 lakh plus one cycle of working capital (max 25% of project cost, not eligible for subsidy); financing pattern: 40% Government of India subsidy, 55% bank loan, 5% beneficiary contribution
Main Benefits: Subsidy-plus-bank-loan combination to set up new coir manufacturing units, along with skill training and marketing support

Scheme Name: Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI)
Social Category Eligibility: Any (inclusive of SC/ST/women depending on cluster composition)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Funds cluster-level development for traditional industry artisans, covering infrastructure, technology, skilling and market linkages
Financial Benefit Details: Up to Rs. 2.5 crore for regular clusters (up to 500 artisans); up to Rs. 5 crore for major clusters (more than 500 artisans); soft interventions funded up to Rs. 25 lakh
State / Geographic Eligibility: All India (500+ approved clusters across 18+ states as of 2026)
Main Benefits: Cluster-level funding for infrastructure, skill development, technology upgradation and market linkages that benefit member artisans

Scheme Name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides a credit-linked capital subsidy for upgrading and formalising unorganised micro food-processing units
Financial Benefit Details: 35% credit-linked capital subsidy (maximum Rs. 10 lakh per unit) for individual micro-enterprises; seed capital of Rs. 40,000 per member for SHG members; support for common infrastructure and branding/marketing for FPOs and cooperatives
Age Eligibility: Not specified precisely; general adult eligibility (18+) implied
State / Geographic Eligibility: All India, implemented through State/UT nodal departments
Main Benefits: 35% capital subsidy for food-processing unit upgradation, along with training, branding and marketing support

Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Subsidises certification cost, improving product quality, market access and eligibility for government tenders
Financial Benefit Details: Subsidy on certification cost: 80% for Micro, 60% for Small, 50% for Medium enterprises; additional 10% subsidy for women-owned and SC/ST-owned units and units in NER/Himalayan/LWE/aspirational districts; additional 5% for SFURTI/MSE-CDP cluster members; Rs. 10,000 incentive for taking the ZED pledge
Age Eligibility: Not applicable (enterprise must have at least 1 year of operations)
Main Benefits: Heavily subsidised quality/sustainability certification, enhanced CGTMSE credit-guarantee coverage, and preference in government tenders

Gender Eligibility: All (dedicated women-MSME acceleration cohorts run in some states)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Strengthens existing MSME schemes (CGTMSE-linked credit, GeM market access, ZED greening) and improves centre-state coordination for MSME support
Financial Benefit Details: Varies based on eligibility/project; total programme outlay of about Rs. 6,000 crore for FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-27, targeting more than 5.5 lakh MSMEs
Main Benefits: Improved access to credit, market linkages (GeM), technology upgradation and greening support delivered through linked MSME schemes

Scheme Name: National Livestock Mission - Entrepreneurship Development Programme
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides capital subsidy for establishing livestock-related micro/small enterprises
Financial Benefit Details: 50% capital subsidy, with the ceiling varying by activity (for example, up to about Rs. 25 lakh for a poultry unit, up to about Rs. 30 lakh for sheep/goat breeding, up to about Rs. 50 lakh for feed/fodder units), disbursed in two instalments
Main Benefits: 50% capital subsidy for setting up livestock, poultry or feed/fodder enterprises in rural areas

Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides interest subvention and credit guarantee support for animal husbandry and dairy/meat-processing infrastructure projects
Financial Benefit Details: 3% interest subvention for eligible entities; loan financing of up to 90% of project cost; beneficiary contribution of 10% (micro/small enterprises) up to 15% (medium enterprises); NABARD-managed credit guarantee fund covering up to 25% of the credit facility for MSMEs
Main Benefits: Interest subvention and credit-guarantee support for setting up dairy/meat processing and animal-husbandry infrastructure

Social Category Eligibility: Any (SC/ST women receive a higher subsidy)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides subsidised, collateral-free loans for women to start small businesses across a defined list of trades
Financial Benefit Details: Loan of Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 3 lakh; subsidy of 30% (general/special category, capped at Rs. 90,000); 50% subsidy for SC/ST women (capped at about Rs. 1.5 lakh); zero-interest provisions reported for widows, disabled and BPL women in some variants
Income Limit: Below Rs. 1,50,000/year (general/special category); below Rs. 2,00,000/year (SC/ST category)
Main Benefits: Collateral-free loan with substantial subsidy enabling women to start small businesses across 88 eligible trades

Scheme Name: Interest Equalisation Scheme for MSME Exporters
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Reduces the effective interest cost on export credit, improving the price competitiveness of MSME exports
Financial Benefit Details: 3% interest equalisation/subvention on pre- and post-shipment rupee export credit for MSME manufacturer exporters; annual benefit capped at about Rs. 50 lakh per Importer-Exporter Code (IEC)
Main Benefits: Reduced interest cost on export credit, improving the global competitiveness of MSME exporters

Scheme Name: Trade Related Entrepreneurship Assistance and Development (TREAD) Scheme for Women
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Combines credit access with training and counselling support for women entrepreneurs delivered via NGOs
Financial Benefit Details: Government of India grant of up to 30% of the total project cost (subject to a ceiling of Rs. 30 lakh) to NGOs for capacity-building; the remaining approximately 70% is financed as a loan by the lending bank
Main Benefits: Combines credit access with training, counselling and capacity-building support for women entrepreneurs

Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides soft-loan/seed-capital assistance to bridge the equity gap for women-owned small enterprises
Financial Benefit Details: Soft loan of up to 25% of project cost (maximum Rs. 2.5 lakh) for projects costing up to Rs. 10 lakh; repayable over up to 10 years including a moratorium period
Main Benefits: Low-cost seed-capital assistance reducing the promoter's own-contribution burden for women-owned units

Scheme Name: Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme for Technology Upgradation (CLCSS / CLCS-TUS)
Social Category Eligibility: Any (special provisions referenced for SC/ST, women, NER, hill states and aspirational/LWE districts)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides a capital subsidy to reduce the cost of technology upgradation for manufacturing/service MSEs
Financial Benefit Details: 15% upfront capital subsidy on institutional finance used for technology upgradation, subject to a loan ceiling of Rs. 1 crore (maximum subsidy of about Rs. 15 lakh)
Main Benefits: Reduces the effective cost of technology upgradation for MSEs through an upfront capital subsidy

Scheme Name: NSIC Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS) / Public Procurement Policy for MSEs
Social Category Eligibility: Any (dedicated procurement sub-targets: 4% for SC/ST-owned MSEs, 3% for women-owned MSEs)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Enables MSEs to participate in government tenders with tender-fee waivers, EMD exemption and price preference
Financial Benefit Details: Not applicable (this is a market-access facilitation scheme rather than direct financial assistance); benefits include free tender sets, EMD exemption, price preference of up to L1+15%, and reserved procurement share
Main Benefits: Every Central Ministry/Department/PSU must source a minimum 25% of annual procurement from MSEs, with 4% earmarked for SC/ST-owned units and 3% for women-owned units; registered MSEs also get EMD/tender-fee exemptions and price preference

Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Supports handicraft artisans through cluster development, design intervention, marketing support and infrastructure
Financial Benefit Details: Varies based on eligibility/project; component-wise assistance for cluster development, marketing support and design intervention. Precise current subsidy/grant figures were not independently verified with an official numeric source during this research and should be confirmed separately
Main Benefits: Cluster development, design and marketing support, trade-fair participation and infrastructure development for handicraft artisan groups

Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Supports handloom weavers through cluster development, yarn supply support, marketing linkages and infrastructure
Financial Benefit Details: Varies based on eligibility/project; component-wise assistance for cluster development, yarn-supply support (via the National Handloom Development Corporation) and weaver training. Precise current amounts were not independently verified with an official numeric source during this research
Main Benefits: Financial and infrastructural support to handloom weaver clusters, yarn-supply assistance, and marketing linkages

Scheme Name: NBCFDC Term Loan Scheme (General Backward Classes Entrepreneurs)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Provides concessional term loans for setting up income-generating self-employment ventures across multiple sectors
Financial Benefit Details: Term loan / margin money loan; the loan amount and interest rate vary by sub-scheme and activity (distinct from the women-specific New Swarnima product listed separately)
Income Limit: Below double the poverty line (older circular cites Rs. 81,000/year rural and Rs. 1,03,000/year urban; reconfirm current threshold on the official website)
Main Benefits: Concessional term loans for OBC entrepreneurs across agriculture, small business, transport and service sectors

Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Facilitates procurement of both indigenous and imported raw materials on credit, easing working-capital pressure on MSMEs
Financial Benefit Details: Varies based on eligibility/project; NSIC facilitates raw-material procurement on a credit basis for member MSMEs. Precise current margin-money requirements and credit limits were not independently verified with an official numeric source during this research
Main Benefits: Helps MSMEs procure raw materials without a large upfront capital outlay, improving working-capital management

Scheme Name: Government e-Marketplace (GeM) - MSE and Startup Enablement
Gender Eligibility: All (dedicated seller category and preference for women entrepreneurs)
Entrepreneur / Business Relevance: Online marketplace giving entrepreneurs direct access to government procurement without intermediaries; includes a Startup Runway with relaxed eligibility norms
Financial Benefit Details: Not applicable (this is a market-access platform, not a source of direct financial disbursement)
Main Benefits: Direct access to government buyers, relaxed eligibility for MSEs and startups under the Startup Runway, and transparent online bidding
